summary: The statement and proof are correct. The dimension-zero, empty-family, and singleton boundary cases produce no counterexamples. All nine initial-segment adjacency counts and their exact lower bounds are valid. The convexity argument establishes the required norm bound, and its use with the nonnegative initial-segment decompositions proves the scalar inequality with the stated direction, including zero vectors. The slices are nested down-sets, the five-term adjacency partition is exact, and induction proves the claimed two-family inequality in every dimension. Setting the families equal gives the stated self-pair exponent. The dimension-one witness has product of cardinalities three and exactly two adjacent ordered pairs, proving optimality of the two-family exponent. No external premises or unproved steps are required.
